question: Describe the auditor's responsibilities relating to fraud in an audit of financial statements under SA 240, including the presumed risks and the required team discussion.
sources: SA 240 The Auditor's Responsibilities Relating to Fraud in an Audit of Financial Statements

points.label: Responsibility for prevention and detection
points.description: Primary responsibility for preventing and detecting fraud lies with those charged with governance and management; the auditor obtains reasonable assurance that financial statements are free from material misstatement due to fraud or error.
points.basis: SA 240, responsibility for the prevention and detection of fraud

points.label: Professional skepticism
points.description: Maintain professional skepticism throughout the audit, recognising that fraud could exist despite past experience of the honesty and integrity of management.

points.label: Engagement team discussion
points.description: Members of the engagement team discuss the susceptibility of the entity's financial statements to material misstatement due to fraud, including the engagement partner.
points.basis: SA 240, discussion among the engagement team

points.label: Presumed risks and management override
points.description: Presume a risk of fraud in revenue recognition, and treat management override of controls as a risk; test journal entries, review estimates for bias and evaluate significant unusual transactions.
points.basis: SA 240, presumed risk of fraud in revenue recognition and responses to the risk of management override of controls

points.label: Communication and documentation
points.description: Communicate identified or suspected fraud to management and those charged with governance on a timely basis, consider reporting responsibilities, and document the risk assessment and responses.
points.basis: SA 240, communications to management and those charged with governance, reporting to authorities, and documentation
